name: Comprehensive International Manual Therapy and Rehabilitation Techniques Directory
source: User requested directory integration with LFS Clinical Driver Console

categories.category_name: Manual Therapy and Orthopedic Manual Physical Therapy (OMPT)
categories.description: Evidence-based joint mobilization, manipulation, assessment of comparable sign. Core for driver identification.

techniques.name: Mulligan Concept and Mobilization with Movement (MWM)
techniques.classification: Manual therapy with active movement
techniques.evidence_level: B (Moderate - strong for peripheral joints, cervicogenic headache, elbow, ankle)

irritability_guidance.low: Sustained NAGs/SNAGs + overpressure, 3x6 reps, weight bearing
irritability_guidance.medium: Gentle MWM with pain-free direction, 3x6, belt-assisted
irritability_guidance.high: Avoid weight-bearing MWM, use gentle positional SNAGs supine if pain-free

techniques.dosage_template: 3 sets x 6 repetitions, sustained glide during movement, pain must be 0/10 during technique (PILL - Pain-free)
techniques.isolation_logic: If MWM improves comparable sign 100% pain-free during technique, joint positional fault driver. Test retest immediate.
compensation_watch: Patient guards against movement, therapist over-glides, loss of pain-free principle
techniques.retest_rule: MWM must improve comparable sign 100% pain-free DURING application. If not, try different glide direction. Retest after 6 reps - need >70% carry over 2min.
techniques.safety_notes: Pain-free rule mandatory. No thrust. Check red flags. Avoid if ligament rupture/recent fracture.
techniques.integration_with_exercise: MWM window: Immediately follow with functional task training in newly pain-free range - e.g., ankle MWM for dorsiflexion + squat training, cervical SNAG + deep flexor activation
special_tests_linked: Elbow flexion MWM for tennis elbow
aliases: SNAGs, NAGs, Spinal MWMs, Peripheral MWMs

techniques.name: McKenzie Method of Mechanical Diagnosis and Therapy (MDT)
techniques.classification: Assessment + repeated movements, directional preference
techniques.evidence_level: A (Strong for low back pain with centralization)

irritability_guidance.low: End-range repeated extensions 10x 5x/day, with overpressure
irritability_guidance.medium: Mid-range repeated movements 5-10x, avoid overpressure, test flexion vs extension preference
irritability_guidance.high: Gentle mid-range 3-5x only, sustained postures, no overpressure. Assess centralization only

techniques.dosage_template: Repeated movements 5-15x every 2-3 hours, directional preference: extension, flexion, lateral shift correction
techniques.isolation_logic: Centralization phenomenon: If peripheral pain centralizes to spine with repeated direction -> discogenic driver. If pain peripheralizes -> opposite direction or stop.
compensation_watch: Lumbar shift not corrected before extension, performing flexion when extension centralizes, breath holding
techniques.retest_rule: Assess centralization after 10 reps. Centralization + improved ROM >50% = directional preference driver. If 1 set worsens peripheralization lasting >10min -> stop.
techniques.safety_notes: Document centralization/peripheralization. Red flags must be cleared. CES, myelopathy caution. Not for high irritability with peripheralization.
techniques.integration_with_exercise: MDT is exercise itself: Patient generates forces. Follow with posture education + prophylaxis. LFS link: MDT can identify extension driver same as lumbar extension comparable sign
contraindications: Cauda equina, severe myelopathy, unable to centralize after 3 directions

techniques.name: Maitland Mobilization Techniques
techniques.classification: Graded passive accessory/intervertebral mobilizations
techniques.evidence_level: B (Moderate for joint stiffness and pain)

irritability_guidance.low: Grade III-IV end-range, sustained 30-60sec x3-4, vigorous
irritability_guidance.medium: Grade II-III mid to end-range, 30sec x2-3, rhythmical
irritability_guidance.high: Grade I-II short of resistance, 20-30sec x2, gentle, no sustained

techniques.dosage_template: Grades: I (loosening small amplitude before resistance), II (large within resistance), III (large into resistance), IV (small into resistance), V (manipulation). Duration 30sec oscillations x3, retest
techniques.isolation_logic: Assess accessory motion vs physiological: PA, AP, transverse, rotational. If accessory limited correlates with painful limited physiological comparable sign -> joint driver.
compensation_watch: Over-mobilizing painful joint in high irritability, wrong grade for irritability, not reassessing comparable sign
techniques.retest_rule: Retest comparable sign immediately after 30sec mobilization. Expect >30% pain reduction or ROM gain for medium irritability. If worsens at 5min -> grade too high.
techniques.safety_notes: Maitland irritability model mandatory: High irritability = high pain early, night pain, lingering. Use APOS (Irritability, Number of pain-free movements, Resistance, Severity). Check vertebral artery for cervical Grade V.
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Maitland window: After PA mobilization L4-L5 Grade II improves extension 40%, immediately train multifidus activation in new range to hold gain
contraindications: Malignancy, infection, severe osteoporosis for Grade V

techniques.name: Kaltenborn-Evjenth Orthopedic Manual Therapy
techniques.classification: Sustained traction + translational glides with 3-grade system

irritability_guidance.low: Grade III sustained stretch 6-60sec into resistance
irritability_guidance.medium: Grade II-II+ large amplitude before/into resistance 30sec
irritability_guidance.high: Grade I-II traction loosening only, short duration

techniques.dosage_template: Traction Grade I (loosening), II (taking up slack), III (stretch). Glides AP, PA, caudal, cranial. Sustained 6-12sec hold or 30sec stretch, 3-5 reps
techniques.isolation_logic: Joint play assessment: If traction improves pain/compression and glide restores limited physiological movement -> capsular convex-concave restriction driver. Use Kaltenborn convex-concave rule for direction.
compensation_watch: Traction too vigorous in acute, ignoring convex-concave rule (e.g., GH inferior glide with shoulder abduction)
No fixation of adjacent segment
techniques.retest_rule: After Grade III caudal glide GH, retest shoulder flexion/abduction - >20deg gain = positive capsular driver inferior.
techniques.safety_notes: Check joint status: hypermobility vs hypomobility. Avoid Grade III if effusion, acute inflammation. Good for apprehensive patients because traction unweights.
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Kaltenborn for peripheral: Traction reduces compressive pain, then immediate rotator cuff co-contraction training in new pain-free position
contraindications: Acute hemarthrosis, hypermobility with apprehension without fixation

techniques.name: Cyriax Orthopedic Medicine and Deep Friction Massage
techniques.classification: Selective tissue tension, deep transverse friction, injection, manipulation
techniques.evidence_level: C (Historical, moderate for tendinopathy deep friction)

irritability_guidance.low: Deep transverse friction 10-15min to tendon healing phase, with Mill's manipulation
irritability_guidance.medium: Gentle DTF 5-10min, avoid if highly irritable tendon
irritability_guidance.high: Avoid DTF in acute inflammatory phase, use education + isometrics instead

techniques.dosage_template: DTF across tendon fiber direction, 10min, 2-3x/week, with gentle stretching. Cyriax manipulation: one-time low amplitude thrust at end-range for specific lesions like tennis elbow
techniques.isolation_logic: Selective tissue tension: Capsular pattern vs non-capsular, inert vs contractile. Resisted tests differentiation: If resisted movement painful but passive full -> contractile tissue (tendon/muscle).
compensation_watch: Friction too aggressive in acute tendonitis, not following anesthesia or accurate lesion location
Missing referral: visceral, psych
techniques.retest_rule: After DTF 10min to lateral epicondyle, retest resisted wrist extension pain - should be analgesic immediate but mild discomfort after 2h normal. If no change after 3 sessions, reconsider driver.
techniques.safety_notes: Avoid over friction in calcific tendinopathy acute. Cyriax injections historical - refer. Selective tension scheme useful for LFS: differentiate contractile vs inert driver
techniques.integration_with_exercise: DTF window: 10min friction reduces tendon pain to allow isometric -> isotonic progressive loading (Stanish). Link to exercise prescription skill
contraindications: Infection over lesion, malignancy, fragile skin, nerve over lesion

categories.description: Assessment and treatment of mechanosensitivity of peripheral nervous system. Critical for differentiating neurogenic vs musculoskeletal driver.

techniques.name: Neurodynamics and Neural Mobilization Techniques
techniques.classification: Neural tension test, slider, tensioner

irritability_guidance.low: Tensioners with end-range + sensitization maneuvers, 8-12 reps x3
irritability_guidance.medium: Sliders only (one joint loads while other unloads), mid-range, 6-8 reps
irritability_guidance.high: Gentle sliders only supine, avoid nerve irritation, pain-free only

techniques.dosage_template: Slider: e.g., median nerve - elbow extension while cervical sidebends away alternate. Tensioner: both ends lengthen. 5-10 sec hold, 8 reps, 2x/day
techniques.isolation_logic: If ULNT / SLR / Slump positive with structural differentiation (cervical sidebend sensitives) and range improves after neural mobilization, neurodynamic mechanosensitivity driver, not just joint. Check adjacent: thoracic outlet may sensitize.
compensation_watch: Aggressive tensioners in high irritability cause flare, no structural differentiation to isolate joint vs nerve
Confusing neural symptoms with visceral
techniques.retest_rule: After median nerve slider 3x10, retest shoulder flexion comparable sign or cervical rotation - >20% pain reduction or +15deg = positive neural contribution
techniques.safety_notes: Red flags: progressive neuro deficit, cauda equina - not mobilization. Stop if numbness persists after technique. Assess irritability of nerve - high = only sliders
techniques.integration_with_exercise: After neural slider reduces mechanosensitivity, integrate with nerve gliding in functional task: e.g., median nerve bias during desk work posture + cervical mobility
contraindications: Progressive deficit, unstable neuropathy, cord signs, recent nerve graft
special_tests_linked: ULNT1 median, ULNT2b radial, ULNT3 ulnar, SLR, PKB, Slump, Femoral slump

categories.category_name: Medical Taping and Kinesiology Taping Applications
categories.description: Adjunctive taping for proprioception, edema, inhibition/facilitation, mechanical correction to hold manual therapy gains.

techniques.name: Medical Taping and Kinesiology Taping Applications
techniques.origin: Kenzo Kase, Japan (Kinesio Taping), various medical taping
techniques.classification: Elastic and rigid taping techniques
techniques.evidence_level: B-C (Moderate for short-term proprioception, limited long-term)

irritability_guidance.low: Mechanical correction with 50-75% tension, rigid + elastic combo
irritability_guidance.medium: Facilitation with 25-50% tension, proprioceptive, pain relief 15-25%
irritability_guidance.high: Lymphatic edema taping very light 10-15% or decongestive, avoid strong mechanical correction

techniques.dosage_template: Facilitation: origin to insertion 25-50% tension. Inhibition: insertion to origin 15-25%. Mechanical correction 50-75% tension, space strip. Wear 3-5 days, retest within 30min
techniques.isolation_logic: If taping correction of scapular position or patellar tracking immediately improves comparable sign >50%, mechanical deficit driver needing taping as proprioceptive cue not structural fix
compensation_watch: Over-tension causing skin irritation, allergic reaction, using taping as only treatment without exercise
No retest after taping
techniques.retest_rule: Apply scapular facilitation tape (lower trap) 25% tension, retest shoulder flexion pain/ROM within 10min - >30% improvement = positive proprioceptive driver
techniques.safety_notes: Check skin allergy, open wounds, DVT risk (no lymphatic taping if DVT suspected), fragile skin elderly
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Taping window: Tape to enable pain-free exercise - e.g., glute med facilitation tape to allow single leg squat training, patellar medial glide tape + VMO activation
contraindications: Open wound, skin infection, DVT, allergy to adhesive

categories.description: Fascial system continuity, Tensegrity-based approaches addressing myofascial chains, trigger points, distortions.

techniques.name: Anatomy Trains Structural Integration
techniques.classification: Myofascial meridians, 12 sessions structural integration
best_for_regions: Whole body chains: SBL, SFL, LTL, DFL, BFL, SL, SPL, DFL

irritability_guidance.low: Deep myofascial work along chains 60-90min sessions
irritability_guidance.medium: Gentle superficial fascia release 30-60min, avoid deep in painful areas
irritability_guidance.high: Very gentle skin rolling + breathing, avoid deep aggressive fascial work

techniques.dosage_template: 12-session series: Session 1 opening breathing, 2 feet, 3 lateral line, 4 spiral line, etc. Each session 60-90min, myofascial release along lines with movement
techniques.isolation_logic: If limited dorsiflexion linked to tight Superficial Back Line (plantar fascia -> hamstrings -> erector spinae), and SBL release improves ankle + lumbar extension together, SBL driver not isolated joint
compensation_watch: Aggressive deep work causing bruising, ignoring irritability, treating without movement integration
Missing ADR border? No
techniques.retest_rule: After SBL release: plantar fascia + calf + hamstring 10min, retest standing toe touch AND ankle dorsiflexion knee-to-wall - both should improve >20% if SBL driver
techniques.safety_notes: Caution with anticoagulants, osteoporosis, acute DVT, skin integrity
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Anatomy Trains requires movement integration after release: SBL release then integrated standing forward bend with breathing + core

techniques.name: Myofascial Release Therapy
techniques.classification: Sustained gentle pressure into fascial restrictions

irritability_guidance.low: Sustained pressure 90-120sec to fascial barrier, 3-5min per area
irritability_guidance.medium: Gentle sustained 60-90sec, no pain >3/10
irritability_guidance.high: Very light skin traction 30-60sec only

techniques.dosage_template: Sustained gentle pressure to restriction, wait for tissue creep 90-120sec, follow release 3-5min per region
techniques.isolation_logic: If thoracolumbar fascia tightness restricts lumbar flexion and extension, and MFR improves both directions regardless of joint, fascial driver
compensation_watch: Too much pressure causing guarding, no follow-up movement
Only local not global chain
techniques.retest_rule: After thoracolumbar fascia MFR 3min sidelying, retest lumbar flexion + extension - need >25% change both directions if fascial
techniques.safety_notes: Check anticoagulants, skin
techniques.integration_with_exercise: MFR window: Immediately integrate with breathing + fascial stretch - e.g., thoracolumbar fascia release + quadruped rock back

techniques.name: Fascial Manipulation Technique
techniques.classification: Deep friction to specific Centers of Coordination (CC) and Fusion (CF) along myofascial planes
best_for_regions: All: mapped points: antemotion, retromotion, latermotion maps

irritability_guidance.low: Deep friction to densified CC point 3min per point, 5-7 points per session
irritability_guidance.medium: Gentle friction 2min, less points, assess pain during
irritability_guidance.high: Avoid deep FM in high irritability, use superficial

techniques.dosage_template: Assessment via movement + palpation of CC/CF, treat den densified points with deep friction over bone or muscle 3min until 50% pain reduction at point
techniques.isolation_logic: FM model: If movement in specific plane (e.g., antemotion knee) limited and CC point palpation hypersensitive (e.g., antemotion knee on thigh), FM driver
compensation_watch: Not finding accurate CC, friction too painful, not reassessing movement immediately
techniques.retest_rule: After 1 CC treated, retest limited plane immediately - expect >50% improvement in that plane if correct CC
techniques.safety_notes: Avoid over arteries, nerves, recent trauma. Friction may be uncomfortable
techniques.integration_with_exercise: After CC release, train specific plane movement - e.g., antemotion CC release + deep squat with antemotion pattern

techniques.name: Dry Needling for Myofascial Trigger Points
techniques.classification: Intramuscular needling to trigger point to elicit LTR
techniques.evidence_level: B (Strong short-term analgesia for myofascial pain)

irritability_guidance.low: Deep dry needling pistoning to elicit local twitch response, 10-15 pistons, leave 2-5min
irritability_guidance.medium: Superficial or gentle pistoning 5-10 times, avoid strong twitch if high sensitivity
irritability_guidance.high: Avoid deep DN in high irritability, consider superficial or not at all, use gentle myofascial techniques

techniques.dosage_template: Palpate taut band trigger point, needle with clean technique, pistoning until LTR, retain or not 1-5min, 3-6 points per session weekly
techniques.isolation_logic: If palpation reproduces familiar pain, weak muscle improves strength immediately after DN (e.g., glute med weak -> trigger point DN -> strength +20% immediate), myofascial trigger point driver inhibiting muscle
compensation_watch: Over-needling high irritability causing flare, not following with activation, missing deep muscles
Unsafe needling: lung near upper trap deep, neurovascular
techniques.retest_rule: Test strength/ROM before and immediately after: e.g., glute med side-lying strength 3/5 -> after DN 4/5 + pain -50% = positive trigger point inhibition driver
techniques.safety_notes: Clean field, anatomy knowledge, consent, check anticoagulants, lung apices (upper trap), contraindicated pneumothorax risk zones. Red flag screening mandatory. Sharps disposal.
techniques.integration_with_exercise: DN window: Immediate activation of inhibited muscle after deactivation of trigger point - e.g., upper trap DN + lower trap/serratus activation to prevent recurrence
contraindications: Patient fear, bleeding disorders, local infection, unstable medical

techniques.name: Dry Needling for Fascial System - Ali Marzok Method
techniques.origin: Ali Marzok, LFS - Fascia as sensory organ
techniques.classification: Fascial layer dry needling targeting fascial densification with neuro-fascial approach
techniques.evidence_level: C (Emerging clinical - based on Stecco + fascial innervation)

irritability_guidance.low: Fascial needling superficial layers along chains, 10-15 points with gentle stimulation
irritability_guidance.medium: Gentle superficial fascial needling, fewer points, avoid deep twitch
irritability_guidance.high: Gentle skin rolling + education, DN deferred

techniques.dosage_template: Assess fascial glide via ultrasound or palpation, needle along fascial planes, gentle rotation, leave 5min, assess glide change
techniques.isolation_logic: If multiple muscles along fascial chain weak/limited (e.g., hamstring + calf + plantar fascia + lumbar erectors all tight) and fascial densification palpable, fascial system driver not individual muscle. Marzok method emphasizes fascia as sensory organ linking LFS driver concept.
compensation_watch: Needling muscle only not fascia, missing chain assessment
Deep aggressive in high irritability
techniques.retest_rule: After thoracolumbar fascia DN 5 points, retest SLR + lumbar extension + ankle dorsiflexion - all improving >15% suggests fascial system driver
techniques.safety_notes: Fascial layers superficial - avoid deep organs. Clean technique. LFS safety gate still applies.
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Fascial DN + immediate fascial loading: e.g., plantar + calf fascial needling then ankle dorsiflexion loading + thoracolumbar fascia chain stretch

techniques.name: Fascial Distortion Model
techniques.classification: 6 distortions: triggerband, herniated trigger point, continuum distortion, folding distortion, cylinder distortion, tectonic fixation

irritability_guidance.low: Strong manual technique: triggerband thumb pressure along fascial line
irritability_guidance.medium: Moderate pressure, gentler
irritability_guidance.high: Gentle, consider deferring strong FDM

techniques.dosage_template: Patient describes pain with hand gestures (finger = triggerband along line, fist = herniated trigger point, etc.). Treat specific distortion: e.g., triggerband - deep thumb pressure along band 1-2min
techniques.isolation_logic: Interpret body language: patient rubbing along line = triggerband; pressing point = HTp; cracking joint = tectonic fixation; deep aching diffuse = cylinder. Treatment matches gesture.
compensation_watch: Misinterpreting gesture, aggressive pressure causing guarding
techniques.retest_rule: After 1 distortion correction, pain should decrease >50% immediate e.g., ankle continuum distortion inverted ankle sprain correction improves dorsiflexion immediate
techniques.safety_notes: Moderate to strong pressure - check tolerance, anticoagulants, fractures
techniques.integration_with_exercise: After FDM correction, load functional pattern that provoked distortion

categories.description: Visceral fascia, organ mobility influence on musculoskeletal drivers, especially psoas, diaphragm, pelvic floor linkage.

techniques.name: Visceral Manual Therapy - Ali Marzok Approach
techniques.origin: Ali Marzok, integrating visceral fascia with LFS driver model
techniques.classification: Visceral fascial release linking organ mobility to motor control driver
techniques.evidence_level: C (Clinical expert model linking visceral irritation to muscle inhibition)

irritability_guidance.low: Gentle visceral mobilization 3-5min per organ, breathing integration
irritability_guidance.medium: Very gentle 1-2min, avoid deep abdominal in acute pain
irritability_guidance.high: Contraindicated in acute visceral inflammation - refer, gentle breathing only

techniques.dosage_template: Assess psoas inhibition linked to visceral irritation (e.g., ileocecal valve region tenderness + psoas weak). Gentle visceral mobilization sustained 90-120sec with breathing, retest psoas strength
techniques.isolation_logic: If glute med weak + psoas weak + lower abdominal tender + eating habits linked, visceral driver causing reflex inhibition per Marzok method. Check dependency: if psoas activates after visceral release without muscle cueing, visceral driver.
compensation_watch: Aggressive abdominal pressure in acute pain, missing referral to medicine for visceral pathology
Neglecting breathing diaphragm as visceral driver
techniques.retest_rule: After gentle ileocecal or sigmoid visceral mobilization 2min + breathing, retest psoas strength and lumbar extension comparable sign - >30% immediate improvement = visceral contribution
techniques.safety_notes: Must screen red flags: visceral pathologies (appendicitis, infection, malignancy) - refer immediately. Check abdominal aortic aneurysm, pregnancy, recent surgery
techniques.integration_with_exercise: After visceral release + breathing, integrate motor control: e.g., diaphragm release + 90/90 breathing with psoas activation then glute activation
contraindications: Acute visceral inflammation, infection, recent abdominal surgery, pregnancy firm pressure, malignancy, AAA
Must have medical clearance for visceral work
special_tests_linked: Thomas test for psoas-visceral link, lower quadrant palpation, breathing pattern assessment

techniques.name: Visceral Manipulation Techniques
techniques.classification: Organ-specific mobility and motility assessment

irritability_guidance.low: Specific organ mobilization Grade I-III, listening hand
irritability_guidance.medium: Gentle listening only, short duration
irritability_guidance.high: Avoid if inflammatory, gentle only

techniques.dosage_template: Listening assessment, mobility testing (push organ), motility (breath rhythm). Treatment: gentle mobilization 3-5min per organ with long lever listening
techniques.isolation_logic: If liver restriction causes right shoulder elevation + thoracic restriction, visceral-organ somatic driver. Indirect assessment for LFS
compensation_watch: Over-treating visceral when musculoskeletal driver primary
Missing medical referral
techniques.retest_rule: After liver mobilization, retest cervical rotation + right shoulder flexion - improvement >15deg suggests viscerosomatic driver
techniques.safety_notes: Medical screening mandatory
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Diaphragm mobilization + breathing retraining + core

techniques.name: Craniosacral Therapy
techniques.classification: Gentle palpation of craniosacral rhythm, dural tube balancing
techniques.evidence_level: C (Low moderate for pain, anxiety, autonomic)

irritability_guidance.low: Gentle still point, dural tube traction, 20-60min session
irritability_guidance.medium: Very gentle CV4 still point only
irritability_guidance.high: Gentle cranial hold for autonomic calming only, short

techniques.dosage_template: Light touch 5gr, assess craniosacral rhythm rate, still point induction CV4, sphenoid, dural tube
techniques.isolation_logic: If patient with high stress, jaw clench, persistent pain with biopsychosocial overlay, autonomic driver, CST may reduce sympathetic tone improving comparable sign
compensation_watch: Claiming structural cranial bone movement > physiologic
Missing red flags cranial (intracranial pressure)
techniques.retest_rule: After 10min CV4 still point, retest cervical rotation + pain VAS + breathing pattern - improvement suggests autonomic component
techniques.safety_notes: Contraindicated ICP raised, acute stroke, aneurysm, recent cranial fracture, severe bleeding disorders
techniques.integration_with_exercise: After CST autonomic calming, integrate gentle motor control + breathing in parasympathetic state

categories.description: Motor control, recruitment patterns, functional movement correction linking to comparable sign dependency.

techniques.name: NeuroKinetic Therapy (NKT)
techniques.classification: Motor control theory - weak inhibited muscle compensated by overactive synergist, manual muscle testing + release + reactivation
best_for_regions: All regions for inhibition patterns: glute med vs TFL, multifidus vs erector, serratus vs upper trap

irritability_guidance.low: Release overactive with massage DN, then activate inhibited with low threshold
irritability_guidance.medium: Gentle release + gentle activation, avoid fatigue
irritability_guidance.high: Very gentle release only + isometrics, defer strong

techniques.dosage_template: NKT protocol: Test inhibited muscle (e.g., glute med) - weak -> test facilitated (TFL) - strong -> release facilitated 1-2min (massage, foam), retest inhibited should be strong -> then activate inhibited with low load 5-10 reps
techniques.isolation_logic: Core LFS integration: NKT provides explicit algorithm for our candidate muscles isolation logic. If glute med weak and TFL overactive, and after releasing TFL glute med becomes strong without activation, proves inhibition-compensation pair = driver
compensation_watch: Only activating inhibited without releasing facilitated
Not retesting after every step
Missing visceral/psychogenic inhibition
techniques.retest_rule: After NKT protocol 1 cycle, retest comparable sign + muscle strength - strength should normalize + comparable improve >30% immediate
techniques.safety_notes: Gentle release in acute, assess if compensation due to visceral or pain
techniques.integration_with_exercise: NKT is exercise prescription: After release + activation in clinic, home program: self-release facilitated 2x/day + activation of inhibited 3x8 low threshold in functional position

techniques.name: Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF)
techniques.classification: Diagonal patterns, rhythmic stabilization, hold-relax, contract-relax
techniques.evidence_level: A (Strong for stroke, ROM improvement, facilitation)

irritability_guidance.low: Resisted PNF patterns D1/D2 with irradiation, hold-relax stretch, 3x 10sec hold
irritability_guidance.medium: Gentle PNF without resistance, rhythmic initiation
irritability_guidance.high: Gentle rhythmic initiation, no resistance, no stretch

techniques.dosage_template: Patterns: D1 flexion (flex-add-ER) extension (ext-abd-IR), D2 flexion (flex-abd-ER). Techniques: Rhythmic Initiation, Repeated Stretch, Slow Reversal, Rhythmic Stabilization, Hold-Relax, Contract-Relax. Dosage 5-10 reps each
techniques.isolation_logic: If patient cannot isolate multifidus, PNF irradiation from stronger pattern (UE D2) can facilitate trunk stability. If hold-relax improves ROM 20deg immediate, muscle spindle driver
compensation_watch: Resisting too much in high irritability, ignoring scapular/pelvic control patterns
Only peripheral PNF not trunk
techniques.retest_rule: After PNF hold-relax hamstring 3x10sec, retest lumbar flexion + SLR - >15deg immediate gain = positive muscle length driver
techniques.safety_notes: Caution with fracture, unstable joints. PNF stretching stronger than static - avoid in hypermobility
techniques.integration_with_exercise: PNF becomes home program: e.g., scapular PNF pattern for serratus training, pelvic PNF for glute training, plus functional mat

techniques.name: Motor Control and Motor Relearning Programs
techniques.classification: Segmental control, deep muscle activation low threshold, motor relearning task specific
techniques.evidence_level: A for low back pain motor control exercise

irritability_guidance.low: Load motor control: Single leg stance with glute med, bird dog with multifidus
irritability_guidance.medium: Low threshold activation: quadr plantigrade arm lift with draw in 3x8, 5sec hold
irritability_guidance.high: Gentle isolated activation supine hook lying, breathing integrated, no fatigue

techniques.dosage_template: Stage1: Isolated activation 10% MVC 3x10, 5-10sec hold, quality with tactile + ultrasound feedback. Stage2: integrate with movement (e.g., multifidus + arm lift). Stage3: functional (e.g., multifidus + single leg deadlift). Frequency 2-3x/day small doses
techniques.isolation_logic: Central to LFS: If weak finding and compensation observed = motor control deficit, not strength. Isolation logic from registry: prone knee flex 90 reduces hamstring to isolate glute. Prone multifidus isolation with draw-in
compensation_watch: Activating global erector instead of local multifidus, breath holding, hip hiking substituting for glute med
Rushing to load before isolated control
techniques.retest_rule: After 5 reps isolated multifidus activation, retest standing extension comparable sign pain/ROM - should improve >30% if motor control driver
techniques.safety_notes: Avoid fatigue, quality > quantity, use feedback (pressure biofeedback for transverse)
techniques.integration_with_exercise: This IS exercise integration skill - progression criteria from low threshold to loaded to functional task integration

techniques.name: Functional Movement Assessment and Correction
techniques.classification: Movement pattern assessment, breaking down dysfunctional patterns
best_for_regions: Whole body: Overhead squat, single leg squat, push pattern, pull, hinge

irritability_guidance.low: Full functional assessment + corrective exercise with load
irritability_guidance.medium: Assess without load, gentle correction
irritability_guidance.high: Avoid full functional assessment in acute flare, isolate

techniques.dosage_template: FMS 7 tests scoring 0-3, SFMA 7 top tier + breakout. If dysfunctional but non-painful -> motor control correction. If painful -> medical screen
techniques.isolation_logic: Links to driver checks: Comparable sign = functional task (e.g., sitting >20min). Break down: Does sitting flexion limitation stem from hip flexor length (Thomas) or thoracic extension? SFMA breakout system isolates
compensation_watch: Only training functional movement without isolating driver first
Load dysfunctional pattern
techniques.retest_rule: After correcting driver (e.g., ankle dorsiflexion), retest overhead squat score - should upgrade 1 ->2 or 2->3 if driver relevant
techniques.safety_notes: Painful pattern = stop and assess red flags. FMS not diagnostic
techniques.integration_with_exercise: After driver identified, functional movement training to integrate: e.g., thoracic extension driver corrected then squat to overhead reach integration

categories.description: Adjuncts to enable pain-free movement window for manual therapy and motor control training.

techniques.name: ANF (Amino Neuro Frequency) Therapy
techniques.classification: Amino-based frequency discs applied to skin to normalize nervous system inflammation
best_for_regions: All with inflammation, edema, nerve hypersensitivity, muscle inhibition linked to inflammation

irritability_guidance.low: ANF discs protocol per injury: e.g., lumbar inflammation protocol discs L4-S1
irritability_guidance.medium: ANF pain protocol + inflammation support discs
irritability_guidance.high: ANF central nervous system calming protocol

techniques.dosage_template: Apply ANF discs per protocol without touching (frequency), wear 72h, replace per schedule. No drugs
techniques.isolation_logic: If chronic inflammation drives motor inhibition (e.g., gut inflammation linked to glute inhibition via Marzok fascial method), ANF aiming to reduce systemic inflammation may improve muscle strength. Test retest after 1h disc application.
compensation_watch: Using ANF as sole treatment without driver correction and exercise
Not assessing underlying medical cause
techniques.retest_rule: After 60min ANF disc application for inflammation, retest comparable sign + muscle strength - any improvement >20% suggests inflammatory/neural driver overlay
techniques.safety_notes: Non-invasive, but screen allergy to adhesive, check medical for inflammatory disease. Not for acute infection fever - refer
techniques.integration_with_exercise: ANF window: Apply discs to reduce pain/inflammation to allow pain-free motor control training following same session
contraindications: Skin lesion where disc applied, allergy adhesive research

categories.description: Dosed exercise to maintain manual therapy gains. Link to LFS retest rule.

techniques.name: Therapeutic Exercise Prescription
techniques.classification: ROM, stretching, strengthening, endurance, power per tissue healing

irritability_guidance.low: Progressive overload 3-4x/week, strength 70-85% 1RM, 3x6-12, endurance 2-3x15-20
irritability_guidance.medium: Low load 2x/week, isometrics if painful, avoid end-range loading
irritability_guidance.high: Isometrics pain-free, gentle AROM, multiple times/day small doses

techniques.dosage_template: FITTVP: Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type, Volume, Progression. Acute: PROM/AROM. Subacute: Isometrics, isotonic light. Chronic: Strength, endurance, power, functional
techniques.isolation_logic: If weak finding, prescribe strength at specific position/bias where weak. E.g., lumbar extension weak at standing end-range -> prone extension prone with multifidus training specific angle
compensation_watch: Loading dysfunctional pattern, too much too soon in high irritability
No dosage progression criteria
techniques.retest_rule: After 2 weeks TherEx, retest strength measure (e.g., hand-held dynamometer) and comparable sign functional improvement
techniques.safety_notes: Screen medical clearance for heavy loading, red flags
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Core linkage: Manual therapy creates window, TherEx holds it. Every exercise must have retest linked to functional task

techniques.name: Corrective Exercise Programming
techniques.classification: 4-phase inhibition, lengthening, activation, integration
best_for_regions: All compensation patterns: e.g., upper trap overactive vs deep flexors underactive

irritability_guidance.low: Full 4-phase NASM: Inhibit (SMR 90sec), Lengthen (static 30sec), Activate (isolated), Integrate (functional)
irritability_guidance.medium: Inhibit via gentle manual not SMR aggressive, lengthen 20sec, activate low load
irritability_guidance.high: Inhibit via gentle breathing only, lengthen gentle, activation isometrics

techniques.dosage_template: Phase1 Inhibit: SMR or manual release 30-90sec overactive (e.g., TFL). Phase2 Lengthen: Static stretch 30sec x2. Phase3 Activate: Isolated activation glute med 3x10. Phase4 Integrate: Single leg squat 3x8
techniques.isolation_logic: CES algorithm matches LFS perfectly: Findings = overactive/weak. Compensation observed = overactive tissue list. Candidate muscles = inhibited list. Use NKT testing to confirm pair then apply CES
compensation_watch: Skipping activation-integration and only rolling
SMR over painful areas in high irrit
techniques.retest_rule: After 1 CES cycle (inhibit+lengthen+activate) 10min, retest comparable sign + functional movement (single leg squat pelvic drop) - improve >30% = positive
techniques.safety_notes: Caution SMR over varicose, anticoagulants, acute injury
techniques.integration_with_exercise: CES IS exercise integration skill - maps directly to report generator exercise program

categories.description: Condition-specific rehab programs that integrate with LFS driver model. When functional task = vestibular, gait, balance etc.

techniques.name: Vestibular Rehabilitation Therapy
techniques.classification: Gaze stabilization, habituation, balance training for vestibular hypofunction, BPPV
techniques.evidence_level: A (Strong for BPPV canalith repositioning, vestibular exercises)

irritability_guidance.low: Gaze stabilization x2 + habituation + balance progressive
irritability_guidance.medium: Gentle gaze stabilization only
irritability_guidance.high: Avoid provoking heavily, gentle only + medical review

techniques.dosage_template: BPPV: Epley/ Semont canalith repositioning 1-3 reps. Unilateral hypofunction: gaze stabilization 2min x5/day, balance 20min/day
techniques.isolation_logic: If complaint dizziness with neck movement vs head movement: cervical driver vs vestibular. Check dependency: if thoracic/cervical extension improves dizziness -> cervicogenic. If BPPV positional nystagmus positive -> vestibular driver
compensation_watch: Missing stroke/central signs (red flag for dizziness)
VBI
techniques.retest_rule: After Epley, retest Dix-Hallpike - nystagmus should abolish. After gaze stabilization, retest dynamic visual acuity
techniques.safety_notes: Red flags for dizziness: diplopia, dysarthria, drop attacks, VBI, stroke signs - refer emergency. Screen cervical artery for cervical dizziness
techniques.integration_with_exercise: After canalith repositioning, integrate balance + habituation + cervical proprioception if cervicogenic component

techniques.name: Cardiopulmonary Rehabilitation
techniques.classification: Graded exercise + breathing training + education for cardiac, pulmonary conditions

irritability_guidance.low: High intensity interval per cardiac guidelines with monitoring
irritability_guidance.medium: Moderate 40-60% HRR, breathing retraining
irritability_guidance.high: Gentle breathing + low-level ambulation with vitals monitoring

techniques.dosage_template: Phase I inpatient to Phase III outpatient, 3x/week 36 sessions, breathing: diaphragmatic, pursed lip, inspiratory muscle training IMT
techniques.isolation_logic: If functional task = breathing difficulty or endurance, or compensation = apical breathing + rib flare observed in lumbar extension test, cardiopulmonary/breathing driver
compensation_watch: Ignoring cardiac red flags: chest pain, unstable vitals
Overload without medical clearance
techniques.retest_rule: After diaphragmatic breathing retraining 5min, retest lumbar extension pain + single leg stance endurance - pain down + endurance up = breathing driver
techniques.safety_notes: Vitals, red flags cardiac: chest pain, unstable HR/BP, O2 sat <90. Requires medical clearance
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Integrate breathing with LFS motor control: 90/90 breathing + multifidus + pelvic floor co-contraction

techniques.name: Neurological Rehabilitation and Neuro-Recovery
techniques.acronym: Neuro Rehab, NDT, Bobath, Motor relearning
techniques.classification: Task-specific training neuroplasticity, facilitation of normal movement
best_for_regions: All if neurological underlying: hemiplegia gait, balance

irritability_guidance.low: Task-specific high reps, constraint-induced if applicable
irritability_guidance.medium: Gentle facilitation, avoid fatigue
irritability_guidance.high: Very gentle, small doses, avoid overexertion

techniques.dosage_template: High repetition task-specific training 50-100 reps/day, split practice, feedback. e.g., sit-stand, gait training
techniques.isolation_logic: If neuro screen positive deficit documented (e.g., weak myotome post stroke), not just inhibition, driver is neurological, requires neuro rehab frame
compensation_watch: Ignoring compensations that reinforce abnormal tone
Plateau without task progression
techniques.retest_rule: After facilitation technique, retest functional task (e.g., walking speed, hand function)
techniques.safety_notes: Check tone spasticity, falls risk, red flags stroke acute
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Neuro rehab integrates with PNF, motor control skills

techniques.name: Gait Analysis and Gait Training
techniques.classification: Observational and instrumented gait correction

irritability_guidance.low: Treadmill training, overground, auditory cues, loaded carries
irritability_guidance.medium: Short distance gait training with rests, assistive device
irritability_guidance.high: Gentle weight-shifting, avoid prolonged gait in high irritability LBP

techniques.dosage_template: Assess stance phase (loading response, midstance, terminal), swing phase. Train weak component: e.g., glute med weakness -> single leg stance training + gait with band around knees
techniques.isolation_logic: If comparable sign = walking pain, gait analysis identifies driver: early heel lift = ankle DF limitation, pelvic drop = glute med weak, trunk lean = glute med weak compensation. Link to hip/knee registry compensation watch
compensation_watch: Trendelenburg, vaulting, circumduction, early heel rise
Missing shoe wear, leg length
techniques.retest_rule: After glute med activation + ankle dorsif mobilization, retest walking pain distance + gait observed pelvic drop - >50% change = driver
techniques.safety_notes: Falls risk, assistive device need, cardiac clearance if elderly
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Gait integration after driver correction: Cue functional task walking with new pattern

techniques.name: Balance and Proprioception Training
techniques.classification: Static to dynamic to reactive balance, proprioceptive challenges
techniques.evidence_level: A (Prevention of ankle sprain recurrence, falls in elderly)

irritability_guidance.low: Bosu, wobble board, perturbation, eyes closed, dual task
irritability_guidance.medium: Firm surface single leg, eyes open -> closed, small perturbations
irritability_guidance.high: Supported balance only, no unstable surfaces

techniques.dosage_template: Progression: Static double leg -> single leg -> eyes closed -> unstable surface -> perturbation -> reactive -> dual task functional. 2-3x/day 2-5min bouts
techniques.isolation_logic: If instability/apprehension finding type, and single leg stance <10sec, proprioceptive driver. Check dependency: Does ankle dorsiflexion restriction cause balance deficit? Fix DF then retest balance.
compensation_watch: Holding breath, hip strategy only no ankle strategy, trunk leaning
Training balance without fixing driver like ankle stiffness
techniques.retest_rule: After ankle taping + dorsiflexion mobilization, retest single leg stance time + Star Excursion Y-balance >4cm improvement = positive
techniques.safety_notes: Falls prevention: support available, no unstable surfaces in high fall risk without guarding
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Balance is integration phase after motor control: e.g., glute med activation -> single leg balance -> single leg squat

techniques.name: Sports Rehabilitation and Performance Enhancement
techniques.classification: Return to sport continuum: isolated -> loaded -> sport-specific -> performance
best_for_regions: All sport functional tasks: Overhead athlete shoulder, runner hip/knee/ankle

irritability_guidance.low: Plyometrics, high load, sport specific drills 4-5x/week
irritability_guidance.medium: Submaximal sport drills, avoid provoking pain, moderate load
irritability_guidance.high: Not sport phase - stay in pain reduction phase

techniques.dosage_template: Continuum: Pain relief -> Motor control -> Strength 70-85% 1RM -> Power plyometrics -> Energy systems -> Sport specific. Criteria-based not time-based. E.g., hop testing >90% LSI
techniques.isolation_logic: If patient high level athlete, driver that is 10% limitation may be irrelevant for ADL but relevant for sport. Use direction/position/bias with load e.g., ankle DF loaded jumping vs standing
compensation_watch: Return to sport too early based on time, not criteria, missing compensations high speed
techniques.retest_rule: Criteria: Single leg hop >90% limb symmetry, Y-balance >94% reach, pain 0 with sport task, confidence >80%
techniques.safety_notes: Criteria progression, load management, red flags, concussion screen
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Final stage of LFS exercise integration - functional task becomes sport

categories.description: Modern pain science integrating biopsychosocial model with physical drivers. Critical for high irritability, chronic pain, fear-avoidance.

techniques.name: Pain Neuroscience Education
techniques.classification: Education reframing pain as brain output, not tissue damage, addressing central sensitization
techniques.evidence_level: A (Moderate for chronic musculoskeletal pain combined with exercise)
best_for_regions: All chronic pain >3 months, high irritability, disproportionate pain behaviors, fear-avoidance

irritability_guidance.low: PNE + graded exposure, 2-3 sessions + exercise
irritability_guidance.medium: PNE gentle, emphasize safety, combine with graded activity
irritability_guidance.high: PNE priority, focus on safety, calming, no aggressive manual

techniques.dosage_template: PNE 30-60min sessions 1-3x, stories, metaphors (alarm system), graded exposure hierarchy, sleep hygiene, stress management
techniques.isolation_logic: If pain behavior disproportionate: widespread, non-mechanical (constant night pain eased? no), multiple regions positive, high fear (Tampa), catastrophizing, no clear mechanical driver via retest <20% change despite multiple corrections, central sensitization driver not mechanical
compensation_watch: Patient high fear-avoidance holding breath, guarding, bracing global
Therapist biomedical language reinforcing tissue damage
techniques.retest_rule: After 1 PNE session + gentle exposure, retest comparable sign - often no immediate physical change but pain 0-10 decreases fear 2 points, willingness to move improves, enabling later mechanical retest
techniques.safety_notes: Screen psych yellow flags but not label. Biopsychosocial approach = referral for psych support if trauma severe. Red flags still medical screen
techniques.integration_with_exercise: PNE is prerequisite for high fear chronic pain to enable exercise: e.g., education that bending is safe + graded exposure to lumbar flexion via time-contingent not pain-contingent

techniques.name: Therapeutic Pain Management Strategies
techniques.classification: Coping strategies, graded activity, sleep, stress, pacing

irritability_guidance.low: Pacing with gradual loading
irritability_guidance.medium: Activity diaries, sleep hygiene, stress management
irritability_guidance.high: Pain calming: breathing, relaxation, gentle graded exposure

techniques.dosage_template: Pacing: break tasks into smaller, time-contingent progression 10% weekly, sleep 7-8h hygiene, stress: diaphragmatic breathing 5min x3/day, mindfulness
techniques.isolation_logic: If functional task pain unpredictable, linked to poor sleep (<5h), high stress, multiple psychosocial barriers, pain management strategy driver alongside mechanical
compensation_watch: Boom-bust cycle: overactivity one day under next
Sleep deprivation
techniques.retest_rule: After 1 week pacing + sleep routine, retest functional tolerance time (e.g., sitting tolerance from 20 to 35min) - +50% = positive behavioral driver
techniques.safety_notes: Referral for CBT if severe anxiety/depression
techniques.integration_with_exercise: Pain management + graded exercise: graded walking 10min daily time-contingent not pain-contingent, then add home program

techniques.name: Biopsychosocial Approach to Rehabilitation
techniques.classification: Integration of biological drivers with psychological (beliefs, fear, catastrophizing, self-efficacy) and social (work, family support, compensation)
techniques.evidence_level: A (Strong for chronic LBP, neck pain, osteoarthritis)

irritability_guidance.low: Address all three pillars, set collaborative goals
irritability_guidance.medium: Validate and address beliefs, involve family/work
irritability_guidance.high: Psychologically informed physiotherapy priority, gentle physical

techniques.dosage_template: Assess yellow flags: Tampa kinesiophobia, PCS catastrophizing, self-efficacy. Use Orebro, STarT Back. Management: education + exercise + goal setting + graded exposure + work linkage
techniques.isolation_logic: LFS model traditionally biomechanical driver, BPS adds: Is patient's belief 'my spine is crumbling' driving guarding/compensation? Test: gentle education + reassurance + movement with support, if comparable improves >30% without manual, belief driver component
compensation_watch: Lumbar bracing due to fear not weakness, walking altered due to work avoidance
Therapist focusing only bio
techniques.retest_rule: After BPS intervention (goal setting, reassurance, graded exposure), retest comparable sign pain and self-reported confidence to perform functional task (0-100% confidence) - confidence increase >20% predicts positive outcome
techniques.safety_notes: Screen severe mental health - refer, maintain therapeutic alliance, avoid judgment
techniques.integration_with_exercise: BPS + exercise: Self-efficacy building - collaborative exercise choice, small wins, functional integration linked to patient-valued activity (e.g., playing with kids)

crosswalk.note: How techniques map to LFS pillars

irritability_to_manual_grade.high: Grade I-II only, sliders not tensioners, gentle activation, PNE/BPS priority, avoid deep fascia/DTF, avoid Grade III-IV
irritability_to_manual_grade.medium: Grade II-III, MWM pain-free, mid-range repetition MDT, sliders + gentle tensioners, gentle trigger point DN
irritability_to_manual_grade.low: Grade III-IV-V, sustained, overpressure, MWM with belt, MDT end-range, tensioners, deep friction, deep fascia DN, plyometrics
